category: A. Same meaning, indirect wording (no reduce/charge/discharge/cap)
note: The battery will not be able to take in any energy from 10 AM to 1 PM while the BMS is recalibrated.
why_this_is_tricky: No 'charge' keyword; 'take in energy' is charging. 'not be able' + 'battery' reads like a generic battery lockout.
common_wrong_interpretation: no_discharge_window [10,11,12] (generic 'battery unavailable'), or no_op (no trigger word).
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Classification from the direction of energy flow rather than from the word 'charge'.

category: A. Same meaning, indirect wording (no reduce/charge/discharge/cap)
note: From 5 PM until 8 PM, the campus loads must be served without any help from the battery.
why_this_is_tricky: No 'discharge' keyword; the battery 'helping' the load is discharging. Talks about serving load, which smells like demand or grid.
common_wrong_interpretation: no_op, or max_grid_window with no number, or minimum_battery_reserve.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Recognising 'battery must not supply load' as no_discharge_window without the keyword.

category: A. Same meaning, indirect wording (no reduce/charge/discharge/cap)
note: Haze from the brick kilns will leave the rooftop arrays producing roughly two-fifths of their forecast between 9 AM and noon.
why_this_is_tricky: Never says 'solar' or 'reduce'. 'two-fifths' is an unusual fraction; 'leave ... producing' means the remaining share.
common_wrong_interpretation: factor 0.6 (treating two-fifths as the loss), or no_op because 'arrays' isn't recognised as solar.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Solar detection from synonyms, fraction normalisation, and 'remaining' semantics.

category: A. Same meaning, indirect wording (no reduce/charge/discharge/cap)
note: The transformer serving campus is derated tonight: no more than 170 kWh may come in from the utility in any hour from 7 PM to 10 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: No 'grid', 'import' or 'cap'. 'Derated' is solar-inverter jargon too, and 'tonight' may trip a future-day filter.
common_wrong_interpretation: solar_reduction (from 'derated'), or no_op (tonight judged as not today).
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Mapping 'come in from the utility' to grid import; 'tonight' is today.

category: A. Same meaning, indirect wording (no reduce/charge/discharge/cap)
note: Whatever happens this evening, the storage bank has to still be holding 110 kWh at the end of every hour from 6 PM to 10 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: No 'reserve'/'minimum'/'at least'. 'Still be holding' sounds like 'hold the battery' (idle) and so like no_discharge_window.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Reserve detection from end-of-hour energy wording, which matches the spec's battery_energy_after semantics.

category: A. Same meaning, indirect wording (no reduce/charge/discharge/cap)
note: Electricians will have the charger's supply breaker open from 13:00 to 15:00.
why_this_is_tricky: Implied restriction: an open breaker on the charger means no charging. No prohibition verb at all; it reads as an FYI.
common_wrong_interpretation: no_op (sounds informational), or no_discharge_window (the 'battery is offline').
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Inferring a restriction from an equipment state.

category: A. Same meaning, indirect wording (no reduce/charge/discharge/cap)
note: Shade cloth is going up over the PV canopy for the 2-4 PM photo shoot; plan on just half of what it would normally give.
why_this_is_tricky: Solar only as 'PV canopy'; the value is 'half of what it would normally give' with no percent sign; 'photo shoot' looks like a distractor event.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Not dismissing an event-flavoured note that carries a real solar constraint.

category: A. Same meaning, indirect wording (no reduce/charge/discharge/cap)
note: The UPS bus for the server room must always find at least 60 kWh waiting in the campus battery between midnight and 5 AM.
why_this_is_tricky: Reserve phrased from the load's point of view ('find ... waiting'); midnight start.
common_wrong_interpretation: no_discharge_window, or hours [0..5] (treating 5 AM as inclusive).
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Reserve semantics from indirect phrasing plus a midnight start.

category: B. Solar value: reduction vs remaining
note: Expect solar to fall 60 percent short of forecast from 11 AM to 2 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: 'Fall ... short' is a shortfall (a loss) but has no 'by'; many readers see 'fall ... 60 percent' as 'fall to 60%'.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Loss vs remaining semantics without the words 'by' or 'reduction'.

category: B. Solar value: reduction vs remaining
note: Solar production will come in 20% below normal from 8 AM to 11 AM due to morning fog.
why_this_is_tricky: '20% below normal' means 80% remains. The number sits next to a lowering word, so pattern logic picks 'remaining 20'.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Percent inversion in the other direction: a small loss must not become a small remainder.

category: B. Solar value: reduction vs remaining
note: A reduction to 70% of rated PV output applies from 10:00 to 12:00 while one inverter string is serviced.
why_this_is_tricky: Contains the word 'reduction' but it is a reduction TO 70%, so 70% remains.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: 'Reduction to X' vs 'reduction of X'; the preposition decides.

category: B. Solar value: reduction vs remaining
note: Rooftop solar will lose three-quarters of its output between noon and 3 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: Verbal fraction plus a loss verb; noon start.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Fraction-as-loss normalisation.

category: B. Solar value: reduction vs remaining
note: Dust on the panels will cut PV output by two-thirds from 9 AM to noon.
why_this_is_tricky: Non-terminating fraction lost; the answer is 1/3, not 2/3. Tolerance matters (0.33 vs 0.3333).
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Loss fraction to remaining factor, with rounding inside tolerance.

category: B. Solar value: reduction vs remaining
note: PV curtailment of 70% will be in effect from 1 PM to 3 PM for inverter firmware testing.
why_this_is_tricky: Grid jargon: 70% curtailment means 70% is thrown away. There is no reduce/drop verb.
common_wrong_interpretation: factor 0.7 ('curtailment of 70%' read as a 70% level).
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Domain term 'curtailment' mapped to the loss semantics.

category: B. Solar value: reduction vs remaining
note: Only one-tenth of the usual solar yield will be available 2-5 PM because of the dust storm.
why_this_is_tricky: Uncommon fraction 'one-tenth'; 'yield' instead of output.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Fraction normalisation with remaining semantics.

category: B. Solar value: reduction vs remaining
note: The solar field will be switched off entirely for inspection from 7 AM to 9 AM.
why_this_is_tricky: No number at all; the factor is 0. Code that tests `if factor:` treats 0 as missing, and an LLM may say no_op because nothing is 'reduced'.
common_wrong_interpretation: no_op, a missing factor, or factor 1.0.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Full outage expressed as factor 0.0, which is a valid value and not a missing one.

category: B. Solar value: reduction vs remaining
note: Solar output will be down by 25% from 3 PM to 5 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: 'Down by' vs 'down to' is one short word apart.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: The preposition 'by' marks a loss.

category: C. Reserve as percentage / fraction of capacity
note: Keep the battery at least 40% charged from 6 PM to 9 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: '40% charged' is a state of charge, so it must become 0.40 x 250 = 100 kWh. The word 'charged' may pull toward the charge-window types.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Percent-of-capacity conversion; 'charged' as an adjective, not an action.

category: C. Reserve as percentage / fraction of capacity
note: Hold half the pack in reserve between 19:00 and 23:00.
why_this_is_tricky: 'Half the pack' has no percent sign and 'pack' is slang for the battery.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Fraction of capacity: 0.5 x 300 = 150.

category: C. Reserve as percentage / fraction of capacity
note: From 5 PM until 9 PM, stored energy must stay at or above one-third of full capacity.
why_this_is_tricky: Third of 240 = 80; a third as a percentage is 33.33, which tests rounding.
common_wrong_interpretation: 33.33 kWh, or 79.99 (rounding beyond tolerance is fine, but 33 is not).
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Fraction-of-capacity conversion with a non-terminating percentage.

category: C. Reserve as percentage / fraction of capacity
note: Battery should be no less than three-quarters full from 8 PM until midnight.
why_this_is_tricky: 'Three-quarters full' = 75% SOC = 150 of 200. 'Until midnight' must end at 24, not 0.
common_wrong_interpretation: 75 kWh, or hours [] / [20] because midnight is parsed as hour 0.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Reserve conversion plus the 'until midnight' end boundary.

category: C. Reserve as percentage / fraction of capacity
note: Maintain 35 percent state of charge or higher from midnight to 4 AM.
why_this_is_tricky: Written 'percent' plus the SOC acronym-in-words; the capacity is 400.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Reserve conversion with a verbal percent.

category: C. Reserve as percentage / fraction of capacity
note: Keep 45 kWh - a quarter of the pack - in reserve from 6 PM to 8 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: Redundant, consistent restatement. A converter may apply the fraction on top of the kWh (a quarter of 45) or report 25 with unit kWh.
common_wrong_interpretation: 11.25 kWh, 25 kWh, or 45% of capacity (81 kWh).
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Not double-converting when an absolute kWh value is given.

category: C. Reserve as percentage / fraction of capacity
note: Keep a 30 kWh floor in the battery from 1 PM to 4 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: When the scenario's base minimum is higher (e.g. 40 kWh), the directive is still 30. Some pipelines 'fix' it to the base minimum or drop it as redundant.
common_wrong_interpretation: no_op ('already covered by the base minimum'), or minimum_energy_kwh = 40.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Reporting the stated value, not the effective floor. The optimizer applies max(base, directive), not the interpreter.

category: C. Reserve as percentage / fraction of capacity
note: The battery must not drop under 60% from 7 PM to 10 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: 'Must not drop' contains 'not' and 'battery', which prohibition patterns pick up as a window type.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: A floor is a reserve, not a ban on discharge.

note: No charging from 0600 to 0900 hrs.
why_this_is_tricky: Military time without a colon; '0600' may be read as 600.
common_wrong_interpretation: hours out of range or rejected; [6,7,8,9].
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Four-digit time normalisation.

note: Grid import must stay under 130 kWh 20:00-24:00.
why_this_is_tricky: '24:00' is a legal end time but not a legal hour. Naive parsers produce 24 in the list or reject the span.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: End-of-day handling: end 24 means up to and including hour 23.

note: Solar drops to 50% from noon till 2.
why_this_is_tricky: '2' has no meridiem; after noon it is 14. 'till' spelling.
common_wrong_interpretation: hours [2..11] or a wrap-around from 12 to 2 AM.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Meridiem inference from the start time.

note: Keep 90 kWh in the battery from 9 in the evening until midnight.
why_this_is_tricky: '9 in the evening' instead of PM; 'until midnight' must end at 24.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Evening meridiem phrase plus the midnight end.

note: Battery discharge is blocked from 12 AM to 2 AM.
why_this_is_tricky: '12 AM' is midnight (0), not noon. Naive 12h conversion gives 12.

note: The charger is down for the hour starting at 3 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: Single-hour window with only a start given. An LLM reporting start 15 and end 15 creates an empty span.
common_wrong_interpretation: hours [] or [15,16], or a guardrail rejection for an empty span.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Single-slot window: start 15, end 16.

note: From 11 AM until 12 PM, solar will be at a quarter of forecast.
why_this_is_tricky: '12 PM' is noon. Naive conversion makes it 24 or 0 and produces [11..23] or a wrap.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: 12 PM = 12, giving a one-hour window.

category: E. Until / through / between and start-inclusive, end-exclusive traps
note: Do not discharge the battery from 4 PM up to but not including 7 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: Explicit exclusivity. A model told 'end is exclusive' may exclude twice and drop 18.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: No double exclusion.

category: E. Until / through / between and start-inclusive, end-exclusive traps
note: Charging is blocked during hours 14 through 16 inclusive.
why_this_is_tricky: Hour slots, not clock times, and explicitly inclusive. In an end-exclusive span format the end must be 17.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Slot-inclusive language overrides the default exclusive clock rule.

category: E. Until / through / between and start-inclusive, end-exclusive traps
note: Grid cap of 140 kWh applies from the start of the 6 PM hour to the end of the 8 PM hour.
why_this_is_tricky: 'End of the 8 PM hour' = 9 PM. A literal reading of '8 PM' as the end loses hour 20.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Hour-slot end phrase converted to the exclusive end 21.

category: E. Until / through / between and start-inclusive, end-exclusive traps
note: Solar will be at 30% between the hours of 1 and 3 in the afternoon.
why_this_is_tricky: 'Between the hours of' sounds slot-like, but these are clock times, so the window is exclusive. 'In the afternoon' supplies PM.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: 'Between' plus clock times follows the default exclusive rule.

category: E. Until / through / between and start-inclusive, end-exclusive traps
note: No discharging for three hours from 6 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: Duration instead of an end time.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Duration arithmetic: 3 hours from 18 gives 18, 19, 20.

category: E. Until / through / between and start-inclusive, end-exclusive traps
note: Charging is allowed only until 6 AM; after that, no charging for the rest of the day.
why_this_is_tricky: The restricted window is the complement of the stated 'allowed' window. It opens with a permission.
common_wrong_interpretation: [0..5] (the stated range taken as the restriction), or no_op.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Complement windows and 'rest of the day' ending at 24.

category: E. Until / through / between and start-inclusive, end-exclusive traps
note: From 10 PM onward the battery must keep at least 70 kWh.
why_this_is_tricky: Open-ended 'onward' runs to the end of the horizon, not to the next morning.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Open-ended window clipped at 24.

category: F. Maintenance implying no-charge vs no-discharge
note: The rectifier that feeds energy into the battery bank will be swapped between 1 AM and 4 AM.
why_this_is_tricky: Pure equipment description; 'feeds energy into the battery' identifies the charging path. No prohibition word.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Maintenance on the charging path implies no_charge_window.

category: F. Maintenance implying no-charge vs no-discharge
note: The battery may soak up surplus solar, but it must not supply any load from 9 AM to 11 AM.
why_this_is_tricky: Mentions solar (a solar_reduction pull) and a permitted charge ('soak up') before the actual ban.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Picking the prohibited direction when both directions are mentioned.

category: F. Maintenance implying no-charge vs no-discharge
note: Discharging is fine, but do not charge the battery between 3 PM and 5 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: Both keywords appear; 'discharging' comes first and the negation attaches to 'charge'.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Negation scope: which verb 'do not' governs.

category: F. Maintenance implying no-charge vs no-discharge
note: Relay testing on the battery's output side, 18:00-20:00: the pack can't push power to the campus bus.
why_this_is_tricky: 'Output side', 'pack', 'push power to the bus': discharge described without the word.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Discharge synonyms.

category: F. Maintenance implying no-charge vs no-discharge
note: Nothing may be drawn from the battery between 5 and 7 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: Short passive form; 'drawn from' means discharge.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: 'Drawn from' direction.

category: F. Maintenance implying no-charge vs no-discharge
note: The battery must not be topped up between 2 and 4 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: 'Topped up' means charged, an idiom with no 'charge' keyword.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Charging idiom.

category: F. Maintenance implying no-charge vs no-discharge
note: Discharge protection test: the battery's charging circuit stays live, but its output is disabled from 7 PM to 9 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: 'charging' sits next to the only prohibition-like word ('disabled'), while 'Discharge' appears only as the test's name.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Which subsystem the restriction applies to (output), not which keyword is closest.

category: F. Maintenance implying no-charge vs no-discharge
note: Charge controller firmware flash 2-3 AM; the battery cannot accept energy during the flash.
why_this_is_tricky: One-hour window in the early morning; 'accept energy' means charging.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Single-hour AM window and a charging synonym.

category: G. Grid-cap wording and reserve/grid confusion
note: The feeder can only deliver 175 kWh to campus in any hour between 5 PM and 8 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: The feeder is the subject; the limit is on supply, not on import, so there is no 'cap' or 'exceed' word.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: 'Can only deliver' as an upper bound on grid import.

category: G. Grid-cap wording and reserve/grid confusion
note: Demand-response event 1-3 PM: the utility will only honour imports up to 95 kWh in each hour.
why_this_is_tricky: Business framing ('demand-response event', 'honour') and the word 'demand', which pulls toward a demand change.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Grid cap from contractual wording.

category: G. Grid-cap wording and reserve/grid confusion
note: The utility is holding feeder headroom in reserve for the hospital; campus grid import cannot exceed 140 kWh in any hour from 5 PM to 8 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: Contains 'reserve' but it is the utility's feeder reserve, not the battery's.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Keyword 'reserve' must not override the subject (grid import).

category: G. Grid-cap wording and reserve/grid confusion
note: Keep grid draw 40 kWh below the 200 kWh feeder rating between 6 PM and 9 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: Two numbers; the cap has to be computed (200 - 40).
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Arithmetic the LLM must do itself because the cap is not stated directly.

category: G. Grid-cap wording and reserve/grid confusion
note: Grid import must stay below 180 kWh from 7 PM to 10 PM; the battery should cover anything above that.
why_this_is_tricky: The second clause describes how to meet the cap and sounds like a battery instruction.
common_wrong_interpretation: Two readings for one note, or minimum_battery_reserve.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: One note gives one directive; explanatory clauses are not constraints.

category: G. Grid-cap wording and reserve/grid confusion
note: Campus must not rely on the grid for more than 110 kWh in any hour from 11 AM to 2 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: 'Rely on ... for more than' is an indirect upper bound.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Indirect upper-bound wording.

category: G. Grid-cap wording and reserve/grid confusion
note: To protect the evening backup, battery energy must stay at or above 120 kWh from 6 PM to 9 PM even though grid import will be high.
why_this_is_tricky: Mentions 'grid import will be high' with a kWh number nearby.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Keyword 'grid import' must not override the subject (battery energy floor).

category: H. Note applicability: today vs other days, cancellations
note: From today until Friday, grid import must stay at or below 180 kWh between 6 PM and 9 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: Multi-day range that includes today. A future-day filter that fires on 'until Friday' drops it.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: A range starting today applies today.

category: H. Note applicability: today vs other days, cancellations
note: Last night's no-discharge window is being repeated tonight, 6 PM to 8 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: Past reference ('last night') that is re-applied today.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Past mention with a present re-application.

category: H. Note applicability: today vs other days, cancellations
note: Tonight from 8 to 11, keep at least 100 kWh in the battery for the hostel backup.
why_this_is_tricky: 'Tonight' supplies PM and means today. '8 to 11' has no meridiem.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: 'Tonight' as a today marker and meridiem source.

category: H. Note applicability: today vs other days, cancellations
note: The charging ban originally set for tomorrow has been moved to today, 1 PM to 3 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: Contains 'tomorrow', but the ban has been moved to today.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Resolving the final date after a reschedule.

category: H. Note applicability: today vs other days, cancellations
note: Solar will be down to 20% from 9 AM to 11 AM this morning; tomorrow should be back to normal.
why_this_is_tricky: The trailing 'tomorrow' clause is about recovery, not the constraint.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Future clause does not cancel today's constraint.

category: H. Note applicability: today vs other days, cancellations
note: Yesterday the feeder was capped at 150 kWh from 6 to 9 PM; that restriction has ended.
why_this_is_tricky: A complete, well-formed grid-cap spec, but in the past and explicitly ended.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Past plus ended means no effect today.

category: H. Note applicability: today vs other days, cancellations
note: The 2-4 PM charger outage announced this morning has been called off.
why_this_is_tricky: Today, with an exact window and a charger outage, but cancelled. 'This morning' is a today marker.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Cancellation semantics.

category: H. Note applicability: today vs other days, cancellations
note: Next Monday, the battery must not discharge between 5 and 7 PM for the fire drill.
why_this_is_tricky: A fully specified no-discharge window on another day.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Future-day filter on a well-formed constraint.

category: I. Distractors dense with energy vocabulary
note: Phone charging lockers in the library will be unavailable from 2 PM to 4 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: 'charging' + 'unavailable' + a clean window is exactly the no_charge_window template. The device is a phone locker, not the campus battery.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Checks the subject (which device) before matching the keyword.

category: I. Distractors dense with energy vocabulary
note: The Energy Club's talk 'Why batteries should never discharge below 20%' starts at 5 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: Quoted title contains a complete reserve-like rule with a percentage and a time.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Quoted or reported text is not an instruction.

category: I. Distractors dense with energy vocabulary
note: Solar-powered benches in the quad will be removed for repainting from 9 AM to noon.
why_this_is_tricky: 'Solar' + window + 'removed'; campus PV output is unaffected.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Solar keyword attached to an unrelated asset.

category: I. Distractors dense with energy vocabulary
note: Please log battery temperature readings every hour from 10 AM to 2 PM.
why_this_is_tricky: Polite imperative + battery + window, but it is a monitoring task.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: An imperative is not automatically a constraint.

category: I. Distractors dense with energy vocabulary
note: The metering team will read the grid import meter at 6 PM and 9 PM today.
why_this_is_tricky: 'grid import' + two times + 'today' form a full max_grid template without a number.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: No number means no cap; do not hallucinate one.

note: no chrging of the batery 2-4pm pls
why_this_is_tricky: Misspelled keywords defeat regex or keyword checks; lowercase, no punctuation.
what_exactly_the_test_is_checking: Typo robustness.

note: grid imprt cap -> 150kwh (18h-21h)
why_this_is_tricky: Arrow, glued unit, 'h' suffix hours, typo.

note: keep >=90kWh in batt, 6pm-10pm!!
why_this_is_tricky: The symbol '>=' carries the whole meaning; 'batt' abbreviation.

note: PV: approx. 1/4 of forecast; 10:00-12:00 (panel wash).

note: Kindly ensure that the battery is not discharged at any point between seven and nine this evening.
why_this_is_tricky: Polite passive; times in words; 'this evening' supplies PM.

note: It has been decided that charging of the battery shall not be carried out between fourteen hundred and sixteen hundred hours.

note: Grid import: max one hundred and twenty-five kWh/hour, 1700-2000.
why_this_is_tricky: Number in words ('one hundred and twenty-five'), where 'and' may split it; the unit is written 'kWh/hour'.

note: Solar output to be reduced by eighty percent between eleven a.m. and one p.m.
why_this_is_tricky: Verbal percent plus dotted meridiems.

why_this_is_tricky: Pure jargon (BESS = the battery system); no verb.

note: discharge NOT permitted 1200-1400
